articles.title: Steve Tandy: Wales boss on tough Nations Championship calls in World Cup countdown
articles.summary: Wales boss Steve Tandy on making tough Nations Championship selection calls as he counts down to the 2027 World Cup in Australia.
articles.body:
After over a year and 13 games as Wales head coach, Steve Tandy is getting used to making tough phone calls and then copping flak when his selections are made public.

Tandy named his 39-man squad for November's Nations Championship on Tuesday, with the 11am announcement prompting the usual tribal responses.

There was delight at the inclusions of uncapped trio Aneurin Owen, Che Hope and Rhys Barratt and recalls for Rio Dyer, Seb Davies, Taine Basham and Gabriel Hamer-Webb.

There was also disappointment at the omissions of Taulupe Faletau, Macs Page, Elliot Dee, Bryn Bradley, Mason Grady and Tommy Reffell, who Tandy later revealed had suffered a knee injury.

"There'll be people out there challenging me on selections," said the head coach, who has now named four squads.

"No-one really says who they would leave out either, it's always the people that should be in! It's something that comes with the territory."

Wales great Faletau still has drive for fourth World Cup

Uncapped Dragons get Wales Nations Championship call

Tandy left his role as Scotland's defence coach to call the shots for his country in the summer of 2025.

He has used 54 players so far and is still casting his net wide despite it being just under a year until the World Cup gets under way.

Tandy will be limited to 33 players for the tournament in Australia but has selected a squad of 39 for the Nations Championship.

"I cop flak wherever I go, that's something I'm getting used to. I get some of that, but you can only pick so many," said the former Ospreys flanker and boss.

"Martyn [Williams, team manager] would have kicked off if I had gone with more, he wouldn't be happy with the budget!

"I'm comfortable in this space and know that we are thorough around our selection.

"There have been some brilliant performances out there from boys that are not in. I've had some phone calls over the last few days that were tough, but I'd rather the boys know where they sit."

Wales counting down the year until World Cup

Will Wales tackle reliance on Williams before World Cup?

Opportunity knocks in World Cup countdown

Wales have just 12 or 13 games until they get their World Cup campaign under way against Zimbabwe.

It would be understandable if Tandy was keen to whittle down his options, but he is still keen to reward performances.

"I'd never give out an opportunity, they've got to earn it, and I think I am pretty clear on the core of our group," he said.

"But this is another opportunity to see someone else in our environment and see what comes out of it."

That is the case with the uncapped Dragons pair of centre Owen and scrum-half Hope, but the selection of their Rodney Parade team-mate Davies was more surprising.

The lock or flanker, in his second season with Dragons after moving from Cardiff, has 17 caps, but has not featured since facing Italy in the 2022 Six Nations.

Wales already have Dafydd Jenkins, Ben Carter, Adam Beard and Teddy Williams in their squad and are highly unlikely to take five second-row forwards to the World Cup, but Tandy is still keen to cast his eye over the 30-year-old.

"You see the athletic ability with Seb and speaking to him there was the emotional outpouring of being involved with the squad," Tandy said.

"We had an alignment camp – a smaller unit gathering – and he came in to get to know them. With that exposure, it's a great opportunity to see boys in our environment."

One in-form player who must wait for his opportunity is Page, who has caught the eye on the wing for Scarlets.

The 21-year-old has scored four tries in four appearances, while he has made nine line breaks.

He misses out with Dyer and Hamer-Webb coming in to join Josh Adams, Ellis Mee, Blair Murray, Tom Rogers and Louis Rees-Zammit.

"Macs has been outstanding but that's where the depth of our wingers and back field is really encouraging," Tandy told Scrum V podcast.

"Look at others - Mason Grady, Keelan Giles, Tom Bowen, all those boys are playing well. Jacob Beetham was outstanding at the start of the season [before injury]."

Dyer was selected by Tandy last autumn and won his 24th cap against South Africa, but missed out on the Six Nations and summer Tests.

The Dragons back has been a threat with ball in hand and, like Scarlets rival Mee, has thrived when chasing restarts and kicks.

"Some of his aerial contests have been better than anyone in Wales," said Tandy.

"Rio has really developed that and his work rate has been outstanding. He thoroughly deserves his recall."

Tandy has fielded five different midfield partnerships so far, and could add to that tally after Owen's call-up.

Ben Thomas started against South Africa in July but misses out because of a calf injury, with the uncapped Dragons centre now pushing for a chance at 12.

Owen, a member of the Wales squad in the summer 2021 after a breakthrough season when he broke up the expected partnership of Jamie Roberts and Nick Tompkins, has been rewarded for club excellence.

"He has been outstandingly consistent and does everything really well. Speak to coaches and they mention his standards on and off the field, how he is the last one off after working on extras," Tandy told Scrum V .

"He has had injuries, and you could argue he could have been in the selection mix sooner, but what I love is that he has kept going and kept getting better.

"He has been so consistent and at a high level, not just seven out of 10 but above that."

Owen is a specialist 12 to rival Joe Hawkins, who is with Scarlets in South Africa to play Stormers this weekend along with Taine Plumtree.

Eddie James is one of the five Wales squad members to stay at home, with Tandy likely to field him in the Nations Championship opener against Japan.

There has been debate about the powerful back's best position - with many feeling he has the bulk for inside centre, where he started Scarlets' first two games of the season - but Tandy is sticking to his guns.

"I see Eddie more as a 13. He can definitely play 12, as we have seen for the Scarlets, but in our team he is more of a 13 who can play 12," he said.

"Louie Hennessey, Max Llewellyn and Eddie, they have big frames and there is lot of interchangeability for the 12s and 13s. We have a nice variety of options there."

Tandy has made his first selection of the Nations Championship, but there is plenty more scrutiny ahead with four team announcements to come.

articles.title: Ireland rugby: Key questions as head coach Andy Farrell prepares to name Nations Championship squad
articles.summary: A look at some of the key questions facing Ireland head coach Andy Farrell as he prepares to name his Nations Championship squad on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Ireland head coach Andy Farrell's latest squad selection this week is likely to stir debate about how his team are shaping up with less than a year to go until the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

On Wednesday, Farrell will reveal his panel for next month's Nations Championship home leg, which includes home matches against Argentina, Fiji and back-to-back world champions South Africa before the finals weekend at Twickenham.

Ireland opened their Nations Championship campaign with wins over Australia and Japan before a 40-21 loss to New Zealand in Auckland.

After November, the Six Nations will be Farrell's only extended period of competitive action with his squad before they travel to Australia for the showpiece tournament.

As ever, Farrell has plenty to consider, with the usual injury concerns and several players pushing for inclusion with strong displays during the opening weeks of the season.

Last weekend was particularly pleasing for Farrell, as Leinster, Munster, Connacht and Ulster all began their European campaigns with victories .

Before Wednesday's squad announcement, BBC Sport examines some of the key questions facing the Ireland boss.

The Ireland squad will be announced at 15:00 BST on Wednesday.

Ireland v Argentina, 6 November, Aviva Stadium, 20:10

Ireland v Fiji, 14 November, Aviva Stadium, 20:10

Ireland v South Africa, 21 November, Aviva Stadium, 16:40

Nations Championship finals weekend fixture (opponent TBD), 27-29 November, Allianz Stadium Twickenham

Farrell will be without some key men in November.

Having missed the July games with Australia, Japan and New Zealand, captain Caelan Doris is still unavailable as he recovers from knee and foot issues.

With Doris already sidelined, Farrell would have been concerned to see Jack Conan leaving Stade Marcel-Michelin with his arm in a sling after the province's Champions Cup win over Clermont on Saturday.

The potential absence of both Doris and Conan could create an opportunity for Sean Jansen, who scored a try on his Test debut against Japan before featuring off the bench in the All Blacks defeat.

Fly-half Jack Crowley remains unavailable because of a vascular injury , and while first-choice scrum-half Jamison Gibson-Park is expected to be included, the 34-year-old has not yet featured for Leinster this season because of a groin strain.

Props Jack Boyle and Paddy McCarthy are still missing, but Farrell can call upon first-choice loose-head Andrew Porter for the first time since last year's defeat by the Springboks in Dublin.

Porter, 30, missed the 2026 Six Nations with a calf problem and, having returned for Leinster in late March, he was ruled out of the July Tests with a similar issue.

Porter's Leinster team-mate Ryan Baird is also available again. The 27-year-old utility forward impressed at blind-side flanker during the 2025 autumn Tests before a fractured tibia forced him to miss the Six Nations. He returned for Leinster late last season but missed the July games.

Popular winger Mack Hansen is also back after an injury-ravaged 2025-26 season comprised of two Test appearances and a single run-out for Connacht.

With Crowley out, Sam Prendergast and Ciaran Frawley will battle for the number 10 jersey in November - and both players have caught the eye in recent weeks.

Prendergast has 17 caps for Ireland but has not had the smoothest introduction to Test rugby. A gifted operator with ball in hand, the 23-year-old's defensive frailties have been targeted by teams in the past and he was dropped by Farrell after a poor start to this year's Six Nations.

However, the Kildare-born out-half has sparkled for Leinster this season, picking up back-to-back man of the match awards in URC and Champions Cup wins over Cardiff and Clermont following displays that have showcased his sharpened running game.

While Prendergast has launched into this season impressively, the opening act of Frawley's Connacht career has been impossible to ignore.

Having moved out west from Leinster to secure regular gametime at 10, the 28-year-old has flourished for Stuart Lancaster's side, scoring four tries and starring in last week's thrilling 45-36 Champions Cup win over Saracens.

Ireland's win over Japan in July was Frawley's first Test start at 10. It would not be surprising to see one or two more next month.

Charlie O'Shea has impressed for Munster in recent weeks but Farrell may feel it is too soon to introduce the 20-year-old to Test rugby, while Joey Carbery could earn a recall despite making only one brief appearance off the bench since rejoining Leinster.

As mentioned above, Jansen is primed to play a key role in the back row, while uncapped Munster number eight Brian Gleeson could be included after impressing again in last week's win over Racing 92 .

Gleeson missed out on a possible Test debut 12 months ago when he was forced to withdraw from the squad with an elbow injury.

Garry Ringrose, Robbie Henshaw, Stuart McCloskey and Bundle Aki will likely make it as centre options, but Jamie Osborne may merit a run-out at 12 having recently featured there in Leinster's win over Cardiff.

In the front row, former England prop Kieran Brookes is pushing for inclusion.

The 36-year-old, an Ireland underage international before earning 16 caps for England, has showcased his solidity in the scrum since joining Munster in the summer.

Can Ireland claim statement Springboks win?

Having lost to the All Blacks in July, beating world champions South Africa less than a year out from the next tournament in Australia would be a major statement.

Ireland have won four of their past six meetings with the Springboks but last year's 24-13 reverse in Dublin, before 22 and 19-point losses to France and New Zealand respectively earlier this year were the latest humbling dust-ups with rugby's elite.

Last year's loss to South Africa was a particularly bruising night for Ireland as they picked up five cards and failed to match the might of the Springbok scrum.

While Farrell later praised his side's response to a chaotic first half which they ended with 12 men, claiming South Africa's scalp would be a major declaration of intent heading into a World Cup year.

South Africa have played six Tests since Ireland's last match against New Zealand. The Boks beat Argentina before securing a 3-1 Test series win over the All Blacks.

They did, however, fall to a 42-38 loss to Australia in Perth on 27 September.
